primary_object_card.object_statement: The bounded packet-166b workhorse task resolves the living-purgatory lineage graph using the ledger native candidate and variation-edge namespaces, then tests one shared one-dimensional basin map independently with Julia Attractors, JAX Diffrax and Optimistix, and a Z3 lower-floor certificate, preserving erased-drive failure and no-promotion boundaries.

source_anchors.quote_or_summary: Resolve finding H with the native lineage schema and build gap-D with one shared map across Julia, JAX, Optimistix, and Z3.
Packet truth supplies the ledger, living-purgatory sim source, purgatory pool implementation, and gap list.
Tool-lego fit probes require promotion_allowed false and cannot promote a lego or downstream scientific claim.

primary_object_card.plain_language_definition: This task has exactly two objects: the lineage graph encoded by the packet ledger, and the fixed-point basin of x mapped to x minus one half of the excess above three. The tools may diagnose these objects but may not replace them with field-name guesses, copied peer results, or broader attractor/manifold claims.

native_terms.lineage node: A candidate identifier from the ledger's candidate namespace.
native_terms.lineage edge: A directed parent-to-child relationship from the ledger's variation-edge namespace.
native_terms.shared basin map: The exact map x -> x - 0.5*max(x-3,0), evaluated independently by Julia and JAX.
native_terms.erased drive: The control map obtained by setting the drive coefficient to zero; it must not satisfy the active convergence/certificate bundle.

weirdness_signature: lineage identifiers and relationship records live in different namespaces
the map has a continuum of fixed points at and below the floor while starts above the floor relax toward the boundary point three
Z3 certifies minimality of the above-floor attractor boundary, not uniqueness over the whole real line
primary_object_card.domain: one packet-local purgatory ledger and source pair plus a finite grid of one-dimensional starts above the floor
primary_object_card.codomain_or_output: two repo-local executable probes and JSON receipts with PASS/FAIL legs and literal claim ceilings
allowed_operations: parse candidate identifiers and variation edges from their native namespaces
construct a directed rustworkx graph and test acyclicity
run the shared map independently in Julia and JAX
use Attractors for Julia basin labeling
use Diffrax for continuous relaxation and Optimistix for fixed-point solving
bind the Julia-measured floor and exact map parameters into a Z3 lower-floor UNSAT check while keeping the Optimistix candidate in the independent cross-engine agreement check
required_invariants: edges are parent to child and endpoints are candidate identifiers
Julia and JAX do not read each other's result files
cross-engine location agreement is checked to 1e-8
classification is tool_lego_fit_probe and promotion_allowed is false
erased-drive control changes the combined verdict
forbidden_substitutions: ledger list position as a candidate identifier
candidate payload fields as relationship endpoints
Attractors package import as basin evidence without a function call
precomputed scalar assertion as Z3 minimality proof
tool-lego fit result as manifold or scientific admission
negative_controls: inject or detect a self-edge/cycle in a bounded graph fixture
set the drive coefficient to zero and require the active convergence/certificate bundle to fail
query Z3 for a fixed point strictly below the declared active floor under the above-floor branch and require UNSAT
primary_object_card.adapter_policy: Rustworkx, Attractors, Diffrax, Optimistix, and Z3 are probes or adapters only. Each must name its exact API, preservation, loss, and kill control before it is load-bearing.
promotion_locks: no whole-packet integrity claim beyond the parsed lineage surface
no global uniqueness claim for the fixed point
no peer-result exchange on the claim path

lateral_mappings.label: rustworkx lineage DAG probe
lateral_mappings.target: PyDiGraph plus is_directed_acyclic_graph over native candidate ids and variation edges
loses: append-only temporal ordering beyond the recorded edges
preconditions: candidate and variation-edge namespaces are identified from source
every edge endpoint resolves to a candidate id
lateral_mappings.kill_control: a bounded injected cycle must be reported as cyclic with one named cycle

lateral_mappings.label: Julia Attractors basin probe
lateral_mappings.target: Attractors.jl basin assignment for the exact shared one-dimensional map
lateral_mappings.kill_control: erasing the drive must prevent the active starts from reaching the boundary attractor

lateral_mappings.label: JAX dynamics and fixed-point adapter
lateral_mappings.target: Diffrax relaxation endpoints and Optimistix fixed-point candidate for the same map
preconditions: JAX x64 enabled before array work
lateral_mappings.kill_control: erased drive must keep at least one above-floor start away from the boundary

lateral_mappings.label: Z3 lower-floor certificate
lateral_mappings.target: UNSAT query for a fixed point below the active branch floor with the floor bound from the Julia-measured finite receipt
preserves: fixed-point equation on the active branch
lateral_mappings.kill_control: if the solver query does not depend on the Julia-measured floor and exact map parameters, demote it to decorative; do not pretend the independent Optimistix approximation is a formal premise

root_constraints: finite bounded carrier or start grid

fixation_breakers: treat a cyclic result as an integrity finding instead of repairing history
state the continuum of below-floor fixed points instead of claiming global uniqueness

loop_contract.repair_rule: repair the first schema, runtime, or control failure without widening beyond the two requested probes
loop_contract.stop_condition: both probes have fresh receipts, or an exact runtime/source blocker is recorded

method_contracts.question_is_not_authorization: A question asks for an answer; it is not authorization to implement unless the user explicitly says to do it.
method_contracts.order_check_separate: Parent-to-child direction and active-map iteration order must be checked separately from field and formula correctness, with each order witness named.
method_contracts.baseline_preservation: When debugging runtime behavior, preserve the exact shared map, grid, and packet source baseline and debug the execution path underneath.
method_contracts.falsifier_first: A Popper pass names the target claim, strongest live falsifier, decisive check, and killed/open/survived classification before agreement.
method_contracts.feynman_testability: A Feynman pass names the operation, the observable measured, and the pass/fail condition.
method_contracts.synthesis_refusal: Synthesis must name the lineage and basin receipts separately and explicitly refuse to merge them into a broader packet-integrity or scientific-admission claim.
method_contracts.human_offload: Resolve with tools before asking; ask the human only for private, preference-bound, or unrecoverable information.

evidence_spine.wizard_runtime: Wizard v4.3 object-preservation guard; v4.2 surfaces are legacy/provenance only.

source_math_locks.preserves: sim-mode Max Assembly, receipt truth, and stage gates
packet-local ledger, lineage source, and audit gap

evidence_spine.claim_ceiling: two local tool-lego fit probes that pass local rerun; no promotion, formal admission, basin/manifold admission, bridge, axis, or whole-packet integrity claim
